results.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
results.content: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.

results.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?
results.content: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.

results.title: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
results.content: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]

results.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
results.content: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

results.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
results.content: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.

results.title: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
results.content: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.

results.title: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
results.content: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.

results.title: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
results.content: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them. [Archive edition, June 2026]

results.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
results.content: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

results.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
results.content: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

results.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
results.content: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

results.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
results.content: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

results.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
results.content: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

results.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
results.content: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.

results.title: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France
results.content: French anti-terrorism prosecutors once dubbed her "the muse of the Islamic State group". On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.

results.title: 🔴 French actor Gérard Depardieu to face trial for alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould
French actor Gérard Depardieu to face trial for alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould
results.content: French actor Gérard ​Depardieu will face trial on charges of raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018, his lawyer said on ​Thursday. Depardieu, one of the leading faces of French ​cinema, has denied wrongdoing in the case.

results.title: Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election
results.content: Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a general election that was called after street protests for affordable housing. Anger bubbled over after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home of seven decades and two decrees to tackle the housing crisis were rejected by parliament. In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.

results.title: 'Europe has two kinds of countries: Small countries & those that haven’t yet realised they’re small’
results.content: “The implications of having the far right in power in Brussels are enormous,” warns Sophie Pornschlegel, Senior Advisor at the European Policy Centre. With elections approaching in several EU member states, including France and Italy, what would a growing number of far-right, Eurosceptic governments mean for the EU budget, relations between European institutions, common legislation and support for Ukraine? Could Giorgia Meloni could adopt a more radical stance? “The whole idea of the EU is to have a common legislation that is then applied in 27 member states. Otherwise, what is the point of having the EU?”

results.title: 'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging
results.content: For Ece Temelkuran, the human condition is "unhomed". Speaking to FRANCE 24, the Turkish author cites the rise of artificial intelligence, climate change and the authoritarian drift as reasons why one may no longer recognise the place one calls home. This feeling of "spiritual homelessness" is something she explores in her latest book, "Nation of Strangers: Rebuilding Home in the 21st Century". Most of all, she highlights the importance of human connection: "In survival mode (...) you live on the kindness of others."

results.title: Israel threatens to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms
results.content: Israel's defence minister on Thursday threatened to forcibly displace one million Palestinians in Gaza if Hamas does not move to voluntarily surrender its weapons, as previously promised.

results.title: EU chief urges leaders to 'compromise' for budget deal by year-end
results.content: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the bloc's long-term budget at a summit Thursday, as Brussels pushes to lock in the plans before next year's French election where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls. "Now it is time for all of the leaders to participate in this debate with an open mind, a constructive approach, and a sense of compromise. Because we need to approve this budget timely. That means by the end of this year," Costa said. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels, Belgium.

results.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports
results.content: French far-right leader ⁠Jordan Bardella faced fresh ​accusations of past antisemitic remarks on Thursday, as French media published an additional ​trove of comments purportedly made in chats from when he was a teenager in 2013. The initial allegations against Bardella, the president of the far-right National Rally party, were published ​by investigative outlet ‌Mediapart in September. It reported that he had made ⁠a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments. Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks. FRANCE 24's French Politics Editor Marc Perelman tells us more.

results.title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
results.content: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.
